items.q: Quot diēs iam sunt cum Iūlius Rōmae nōn fuit?
items.en: How many days is it now since Julius was last in Rome?
items.hint: a numeral with diēs in the nominative; Rōmae is the locative

items.q: Quandō aliquis Iūliō dē rēbus urbānīs scrībet?
items.en: When will anyone write to Julius about city affairs?
items.hint: nisi + future perfect (scrīpseris) with a future main verb

items.q: Quōmodo Iūlius facile aliquid novī cognōscere potest?
items.en: How can Julius easily learn some news?
items.hint: per + accusative; aliquid novī has a partitive genitive

items.q: Ubi Cornēlius herī servum Iūliī vīdit?
items.en: Where did Cornelius see Julius' slave yesterday?
items.hint: in + ablative for place where (in viā Latīnā)

items.en: What does Julius ask Cornelius?
items.hint: an indirect question with the present subjunctive (sit); eī is a dative of possession

items.en: Why does Cornelius always forget names?
items.hint: a nam clause with a dative of possession (mihi est = I have); oblīvīscor is deponent

items.en: What kind of king was Midas?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative agreeing with rēx

items.en: What power does Midas wish for himself?
items.hint: a gerund in the genitive (mūtandī) with its own object clause; quidquid + future perfect

items.q: Cūr Midās famē et sitī moriēbātur?
items.en: Why was Midas dying of hunger and thirst?
choices: quia Bacchus eī cibum nōn dabat
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive (fieret); famē et sitī are ablatives of cause

items.en: What did the wretched king pray the god to do?
items.hint: ōrāvit ut + imperfect subjunctive (an indirect command after a past verb)

items.en: What did Bacchus advise Midas to do?
items.hint: suādeō takes the dative (eī) and ut + imperfect subjunctive passive (lavārētur)

items.q: Quid Apollō effēcerat ut Midās habēret?
items.en: What had Apollo caused Midas to have?
items.hint: effēcerat ut + imperfect subjunctive; tap the accusative object of habēret

items.q: Quot servōs fīdōs Iūlius in familiā suā esse crēdit?
items.en: How many faithful slaves does Julius believe there are in his household?
items.hint: the numeral in the accusative inside an indirect statement (that only … slave is faithful)

items.q: Quālis est Mēdus, ut Iūlius dīcit?
items.en: What is Medus like, according to Julius?
items.hint: a superlative with a partitive genitive (omnium)

items.en: When will Medus be nailed to a cross?
items.hint: nisi + future perfect (reddiderit) with a future passive main verb

items.q: Cūr difficile erit servum fugitīvum Rōmae reperīre?
items.en: Why will it be hard to find a runaway slave in Rome?
items.hint: the correlatives tot … quot ('as many … as')

items.en: Where does Aemilia believe Medus is hiding?
items.hint: apud + accusative ('at the house of'); the clause is an indirect statement (eum … latēre)

items.en: To whom will Julius give a large reward?
items.hint: a dative eī with a relative clause in the future perfect (retrāxerit)

items.en: What does Aemilia urge her husband to be?
items.hint: suādet ut + present subjunctive; the direct command that follows uses nōlī + infinitive

items.en: What kind of master do slaves hate?
items.hint: an accusative adjective standing for dominum sevērum; ōdērunt is perfect in form, present in meaning

items.en: Do the slaves hate Julius?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; quidem … nec vērō contrasts the two verbs

items.q: Quālis dominus est Iūlius, ut ipse dīcit?
items.en: What kind of master is Julius, as he himself says?
items.hint: a predicate adjective in the nominative

items.en: It isn't allowed to kill someone else's slave, is it?
items.hint: num expects 'no'; licet takes an infinitive as its subject

items.en: Who wrote laws for the Athenians?
items.hint: the nominative subject; Athēniēnsibus is a dative of the receiver

items.q: Cūr Mānlius fīlium suum necārī iussit?
items.en: Why did Manlius order his own son to be killed?
items.hint: a quia clause with the pluperfect; necārī is a passive infinitive after iussit

items.q: Quid dē patre quī īnfantem exposuit Aemilia cēnset?
items.en: What does Aemilia think about a father who has exposed an infant?
items.hint: a gerundive with est expressing obligation ('must be killed'); tap the gerundive

items.en: What punishment has been established for slaves?
items.hint: id supplicium refers back to the infinitive phrase; cruce is an ablative of means

items.en: What had King Priam ordered the slave to do?
items.hint: imperāverat ut + imperfect subjunctive; the sentence ends with a gerundive (servō faciendum est)

items.q: Quam fēminam Paris ā marītō Menelāō abdūxit?
items.en: Which woman did Paris carry off from her husband Menelaus?
items.hint: the accusative object of abdūxit, with an apposition (fēminam omnium pulcherrimam)

items.q: Quid nunc faciendum est, ut Orontēs clāmat?
items.en: What must be done now, as Orontes shouts?
items.hint: a gerundive with est expressing obligation (the passive periphrastic)

items.q: Quid faciendum est, ut Cornēlius dīcit?
items.en: What must be done, according to Cornelius?
items.hint: an impersonal gerundive with est ('there must be silence')

items.en: Who should perish, as Orontes sings?
items.hint: pereat is a jussive subjunctive ('may he perish'); the subject is a relative clause

items.q: Quō Orontēs priusquam carmen fīnit lābitur?
items.en: Where does Orontes slip to before finishing his song?
items.hint: sub + accusative for motion to a place under; lābitur is deponent
